conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User primary keys differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: Every user id is a uuid. B's integer ids are re-keyed during import and kept in legacy_id until the import is checked (D03).

conflicts.subject: GET /api/users/{} response
conflicts.detail: GET /api/users/{} response fields disagree (id: A uuid, B integer)
solutions: Define one request and response shape and convert at the edges
Version the endpoint if existing clients need the old shape
conflicts.recommended: One contract per endpoint, written into the API spec

resolution.decision: One user shape: {id: uuid, email, name, role, can_approve}. B's full_name maps to name (D05).

conflicts.subject: GET /api/users/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/users/{} uses different auth (A: session, B: bearer)
solutions: Put every endpoint behind the one auth system the architecture chooses
conflicts.recommended: Same auth scheme for every endpoint

resolution.decision: Every endpoint uses the one cookie session (D02).

conflicts.subject: provider
conflicts.detail: Identity providers differ (A: self; B: self; C: google)
solutions: Choose one identity provider and migrate accounts to it
Link accounts by verified email during migration
conflicts.recommended: One identity system for the unified app

resolution.decision: Team Hub runs its own accounts now (email and password). Google sign-in (M03) is deferred and will use the user's own Google OAuth app when picked up.

conflicts.subject: roles
conflicts.detail: Role sets differ (A: member, owner; B: admin, approver, requester; C: admin, member)
solutions: Map every source role to a unified role set and write the mapping down
Model special powers (such as approving) as permissions, not extra roles
conflicts.recommended: One role set plus explicit permissions; map every source role

resolution.decision: Roles owner, admin, member plus an approve permission. A owner->owner, A member->member, B admin->admin, B requester->member, B approver->member with approve, C admin->admin, C member->member (D04).

conflicts.subject: /login
conflicts.detail: Route /login is used by A: A-S01, B: B-S01
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

resolution.decision: One sign-in screen at /login for every user (the example ships the API; the UI is out of scope).

conflicts.subject: /settings
conflicts.detail: Route /settings is used by A: A-S05, B: B-S04
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

resolution.decision: One /settings screen with account and notification sections.

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: cookie; B: jwt-header)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: http-only cookie sessions, 30 minutes idle, for every client (D02).

conflicts.subject: closing-tasks-with-approvals
conflicts.detail: In A anyone allowed to edit a task can move it to done at any time. B's approvals were standalone. Once approvals attach to tasks, a task could be closed while its approval is still pending.
solutions: Block moving a task to done while it has a pending approval
Allow it and cancel the pending approval automatically
Allow it and only warn
conflicts.recommended: Block moving to done while an approval is pending; the approver decides first

resolution.decision: Block moving a task to done while it has a pending approval. Implemented as a status guard the approvals module registers with tasks.

conflicts.subject: user.id
conflicts.detail: User.id types differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: Same decision as database:primary-key:user: uuid (D03).

conflicts.subject: node
conflicts.detail: node: A uses >=18, B uses 16.x
solutions: Target one runtime version that every kept feature can run on
Upgrade the source code that needs the older runtime
conflicts.recommended: Pick the newest runtime version the kept features support

resolution.decision: Not applicable: Team Hub is built on Python 3.8+ with the standard library (D01); no source code is carried over.

conflicts.subject: react
conflicts.detail: react: A uses ^18.2.0, B uses ^17.0.2
solutions: Standardise on the newer major version and update the code that used the older one
Keep the older version only if a kept feature cannot move yet, and isolate it
conflicts.recommended: Use one version, normally the newer major, in the unified app

resolution.decision: Not applicable: no React code is carried over (D01).

conflicts.subject: GET /api/users/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/users/{} versions differ (A: none, B: v1)
solutions: Start the unified API at one version
Keep a compatibility layer for old clients
conflicts.recommended: One versioning scheme for the unified API

resolution.decision: One unversioned /api while there are no outside clients (D05).

conflicts.subject: GET /api/users/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/users/{} exists in A: /api/users/:id, B: /api/v1/users/:id
solutions: Keep one endpoint and adapt clients of the other
Keep both under different paths if they serve different needs
conflicts.recommended: One endpoint per job in the unified API

resolution.decision: One GET /api/me for the signed-in user; user listing waits for an admin screen.

conflicts.subject: methods
conflicts.detail: Sign-in methods differ (A: password; B: password; C: google-oauth)
solutions: Offer the union of kept sign-in methods through one identity system
Drop sign-in methods no kept feature needs
conflicts.recommended: One identity system that offers the sign-in methods kept features need

resolution.decision: Password now; Google later with M03.

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User exists in A:User, B:User; fields not shared: created_at (only A), password_hash (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: One users table with the union of fields kept features use (D03).

conflicts.subject: react-dom
conflicts.detail: react-dom: A uses ^18.2.0, B uses ^17.0.2
solutions: Standardise on the newer major version and update the code that used the older one
Keep the older version only if a kept feature cannot move yet, and isolate it
conflicts.recommended: Use one version, normally the newer major, in the unified app

resolution.decision: Not applicable (D01).

conflicts.subject: button
conflicts.detail: button variants differ (A: ghost, primary; B: danger, primary, secondary)
solutions: One component with the union of variants the kept screens use
conflicts.recommended: One component in the design system

resolution.decision: Not applicable to the API-only example; a UI would use one Button with primary, secondary, ghost and danger.

conflicts.subject: date-library
conflicts.detail: Several date librarys: dayjs (A); moment (B)
solutions: Keep one library for this job and replace calls to the others
conflicts.recommended: Keep one library per job

resolution.decision: Not applicable (D01): Python's datetime is used.

conflicts.subject: http-client
conflicts.detail: Several HTTP clients: axios (A); node-fetch (B)
solutions: Keep one library for this job and replace calls to the others
conflicts.recommended: Keep one library per job

resolution.decision: Not applicable (D01).

changes: re-key rows to one primary key type (A: uuid, B: integer) and rewrite foreign keys that point at them
convert id to one type (A: uuid, B: integer)
add fields that only some sources have: created_at (only A), password_hash (only A)
